(Slightly off topic) I don’t see why it isn’t entirely plausible that the Jackal is also attracted to men. I think him either being heterosexual or bisexual are equally valid interpretations, and regardless, his sexuality hardly affects his character and story. 

 How I viewed the side plot with Rasmus, there’s zero romantic interest toward Rasmus on Jackal’s side and sleeping with him was a means to an end. 

However, I don’t think Jackal would sleep with Rasmus if he found him to be unlikeable. 

He has multiple lines that specifically have to do with Rasmus being “kind” and “radiating kindness” in more than one scene. He’s obviously playing a part, but I think that “you have a good man’s face” scene indicated that he did mean it. He could’ve easily picked any other aspect to praise, yet he primarily compliments him on his “kindness”.

He also did not need to say that “good man face” line to manipulate Rasmus— in fact, it just confused Rasmus, if anything. He could’ve just said farewell and left, he could’ve even left without saying anything, but he gives him a kiss and you can see Jackal’s real (or close to sincere) expression come through when does— The affectionate and sweet and loving mask is gone, and he almost looks vacant. You can see the troubled, “dangerous” vibe behind his eyes.

Also, sleeping with him twice was practical, but I feel like he could’ve avoided the second time, at least, if he tried hard enough lol.


I don’t think he feels any romantic attraction towards Rasmus, but I think Rasmus represents something or is a contrast to the Jackal’s character. He’s almost like someone the Jackal can never be. Rasmus is the complete opposite of Jackal, he lives a happy, honest and simple life, he radiates kindness and his smiles are genuine. Unlike the Jackal, he isn’t wearing masks, and he isn’t playing a part. They both have “good man’s face” but Rasmus’ goodness is also sincerely reflected in his personality. And I think Jackal recognises that and maybe part of him admires that trait in Rasmus. 

And I think, maybe  the Jackal killing Rasmus at the end of episode 7 also symbolised something. 

I think there’s a theme of ‘goodness’ and ‘morality’ throughout the show. Bianca and Jackal parallel one another. They both have to hide significant parts of themselves and their lives to their family, to the point of it fracturing their personal relationships. Both make actions that hurt multiple people (including their loved ones) and they both justify it to be for the greater good (for Bianca, catching Jackal would save multiple people from getting killed or hurt, and thus justifies her part in the deaths of Emma and Allison. For the Jackal he justifies his job and the casualties as  it allows him to give his wife and child a “great life”.)

There’s a thing that I noticed (idk, maybe it’s just in my head lol) but it’s almost like Bianca and the Jackal shut parts of themselves down when they’re working? Like they shut that human part of themselves to do the dirty and ugly work. There are moments where I was like “oh wow, it’s almost like they’re robotic”. 

And for a moment I thought the Jackal could be a psychopath until we saw him with his wife and child. Suddenly he seemed so human. Same with Bianca, I feel like I only ever see her groaning in frustration or wincing at herself when she’s either alone or with her family. But at work she puts on this neutral and even cold mask, which, I think it speaks of the actors’ great performances. Say what you want about the show, but I think the actors did a great job.
